fixes.replace: Before any wiring work, a qualified technician should isolate and verify the power, photograph the original terminals and check the wiring at the equipment board or zone panel; line-voltage and 24-volt products are not interchangeable.

fixes.find: Many smart thermostats do, though compatible adapters or an unused conductor may solve it. We verify at the equipment, not just behind the wall plate.
fixes.replace: Many smart thermostats need a common (C) wire for steady power. Depending on the model, the manufacturer's approved adapter or a spare conductor may solve it, but a spare wire has to be verified at the equipment, not just behind the wall plate, and power-stealing models can behave erratically on some systems. The equipment model, the existing control and any wiring notes help a technician choose the right option.
fixes.why: MAJOR 5: model-specific adapter, spare-conductor and power-stealing guidance; pronoun before brand

fixes.find: The mapped review set includes a challenging two-stage furnace and thermostat installation in a condo utility closet, evidence that controls have to match the equipment and space.
fixes.replace: A two-stage furnace needs a control set up for both stages, and a condo utility closet or zone panel adds its own limits, so a sound installation tests every mode against the actual equipment.
